title: Redwood data retention & PII controls demo - Mariner Financial
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Mariner Financial through Console, API toggles, and Optimize features for data handling: request-storage toggles, automatic redaction, PII detection rules, SOC2/KMS notes. Customer asked about granular per-route storage, audit logs, on-prem controls, and a PoC benchmark. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share recording and policy doc, set up 2-week pilot with request-storage off for sensitive routes.
next_steps: Samir to send SOC2 + security whitepaper and KMS integration guide by 2026-03-08
Jenna to share demo recording and sample config JSON for per-route retention by 2026-03-07
Schedule POC kickoff (2-week) to run latency/cost benchmarks week of 2026-03-16
Customer to provide a list of 3 sensitive routes to exclude from request storage
action_items: Samir Patel: Send security + SOC2 docs (due 2026-03-08)
Jenna Liu: Export demo recording and example config for per-route retention (due 2026-03-07)
Mike Carter: Share three sensitive API routes to exclude from storage (no later than 2026-03-13)
Victor Huang: Provide representative workload traces for benchmark (due 2026-03-12)
transcript:
Meeting header: Date/time: 2026-03-06 15:00 UTC; Duration: 56 minutes; Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Liu (Redwood SE), Mike Carter (Mariner Head of Infra), Priya Rao (Security), Daniel Kim (Product), Sara Lopez (Legal), Victor Huang (ML).

Summary: Redwood demo of Data Retention controls across API + Console + Optimize focused on PII redaction, per-route request storage toggles, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logging. Customer asked clarifying q's on per-tenant vs per-route controls, SLA impacts, and proof-of-concept steps.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood i'm the AE on this account. big thank you to mike and team for the time. jenna is our se, she'll run through the console and the deeper controls. feel free to interrupt.
[00:17] Mike: yeah thanks samir, we've got priya and victor and daniel on sara dropped in for the legal bit. we're most interested in how you handle request data, retention, and specifically PII.
[00:30] Jenna: great, i'll share my screen, i'm going to open the console and start with the global data settings. just a note: transcription may have small typos, but i'll try to call out exact field names.
[01:02] Jenna: first panel is under Settings > Data Handling. we have a toggle for "Store requests" which is global, then per-route overrides. global=on by default for hosted tenants, but you can flip it off for specific routes or models.
[01:38] Priya: quick q \u2014 if global is on, but we set a route to off, does that still write anything to logs for debugging context? like error logs or traces?
[01:50] Jenna: good question. by default we still emit minimal operational logs (error-level) that do not include request content. full request bodies are not stored if you set per-route store_requests=false. we do keep metadata: timestamps, request id, route id, latency.
[02:20] Jenna: there's also a "Redaction rules" section. you can enable automatic PII detection or add custom regex patterns. auto-detection uses our heuristic model it's not perfect, so we recommend custom patterns for regulated fields (account numbers, ssn, payment tokens).
[02:55] Victor: how does the redaction actually work \u2014 is it tokenization or replacement? what's returned in logs?
[03:05] Jenna: we replace detected spans with a deterministic placeholder like [REDACTED_PII]. you can also choose to hash the value (sha256) if you need a stable pseudonym for correlation. hashing requires KMS integration if you want customer-managed keys.
[03:30] Daniel: and where are these logs stored, s3? do you keep them inside redwood services or send them to our s3?
[03:40] Jenna: by default request storage is in our encrypted blob store in the region. we have connectors to stream logs to customer-owned S3/GCS via a push or on-demand batch export. for Private deployments obviously it stays in your VPC/on-prem.
[04:05] Priya: what's retention windows look like \u2014 can we set TTLs per-route? per-environment?
[04:15] Jenna: yep. retention can be set globally, per-route, and per-tenant. typical options are 7/30/90/365 days or indefinite. you can also set custom TTLs. when an object hits TTL it's deleted and tombstoned in metadata; we record deletion events in audit logs.
[04:45] Sara: legal question \u2014 do you provide proof of deletion for compliance audits?
[04:52] Samir: we include deletion audit events with timestamps and the request id; for Private installs you can run deeper forensics. we'll include language in the security pack.
[05:10] Mike: performance impact \u2014 toggling store_requests off \u2014 does that improve latency? and does disabling redaction save CPU?
[05:20] Jenna: small effect. storing requests does add some I/O overhead; for large scale it's measurable. redaction runs an additional pass on the request payload; however the main tokenization / inference cost is unchanged. Optimize can recommend batch sizes and cache settings if you want to minimize cost.
[05:46] Jenna: i'll switch to the API. there's a request-level param: "store_requests": true|false and "redact": auto|off|custom. for streaming we also support header-level directives.
[06:10] Victor: can we set default via SDK? like when our backend calls the API can the sdk set store_requests=false for certain routes automatically?
[06:20] Jenna: yes, the SDK exposes the same flags and supports route-level configs. we also support per-customer policy via the control plane \u2014 e.g., a policy that sets store_requests=false for /payments/* routes.
[06:38] Priya: about the automatic PII detector \u2014 false negatives worry me. do you have an audit mode?
[06:45] Jenna: we do. audit-mode logs detected spans to a separate audit bucket (no request bodies) so you can tune rules before enabling redaction live. it's useful for running against a sample dataset.
[07:05] Samir: worth noting: in Dedicated and Private deployments you can run the PII detector model on-prem which avoids sending any content to Redwood hosted models.
[07:22] Daniel: what about embeddings? if we create embeddings from text that contains PII, are those treated as request data?
[07:30] Jenna: yes, embeddings are request artifacts. same storage toggles apply. also Optimize has settings to avoid storing embeddings, or to hash them if you need linkage without storing raw text.
[07:55] Mike: KMS integration \u2014 we use AWS KMS and a customer-managed key. can we configure Redwood to encrypt request blobs with our key?
[08:05] Jenna: yes. for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer keys via KMS. in Private you manage keys fully. we document the key rotation and access patterns in the pack.
[08:25] Priya: audit logs \u2014 where do they live, how long, and are they immutable?
[08:32] Jenna: audit logs are stored in a write-once append store for the retention window. we can push them to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and they contain event-level info: admin changes, deletion events, login events. they do not contain redacted request bodies.
[08:55] Jenna: quick demo: i'll create a route called /payments/charge and override storage: store_requests=false, retention=7 days, redaction=auto + custom regex for PAN.
[09:20] [screen shows Console] Jenna: navigating to Routes > /payments/charge > Data. toggle is here; you can add regexes. adding pattern for 4-digit-4-digit-4-digit with hyphens. save. notice the policy preview shows affected routes and whether it's applied to subroutes.
[09:55] Daniel: is policy evaluation synchronous? if we update a rule does it affect in-flight requests?
[10:02] Jenna: rule changes are applied in near real-time, a few seconds for config propagation. in-flight requests are evaluated with the policy version active at request start. there is a version history in the Console.
[10:25] Samir: let's talk about the CLI/infra side: for a PoC we'll provision a dedicated project with limited capacity and run a sample workload. jenna will provide a sample agent token and config.
[10:40] Mike: for the PoC we want to ensure that three sensitive routes never have request bodies stored. can we test this?
[10:50] Jenna: yes \u2014 we have an ingestion check tool that will run a set of requests and then attempt to retrieve them from the store. we'll run it as part of the test plan.
[11:10] Victor: about deletion \u2014 if a request is deleted and later we need to re-run a debug, is there any recovery?
[11:18] Jenna: deleted request bodies are unrecoverable after TTL expiration. we record metadata and deletion events but not the content. for longer retention you can set a manual retention or export to your S3 before deletion.
[11:35] Priya: legal \u2014 we may need guaranteed deletion for 3rd-party auditors. what's the SLA around deletion?
[11:43] Samir: we provide deletion logs with timestamps and request ids; for Private we can give stronger attestations. we'll include a sample attestation template in the security pack.
[12:00] Sara: also curious about role-based access to the Console \u2014 can we hide redaction rules from developers?
[12:08] Jenna: yes, RBAC is supported. roles can be scoped to read-only, data-admin, infra-admin, etc. we also support SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[12:30] Samir: switching briefly to Optimize \u2014 some customers use retention knobs to reduce costs. Optimize will analyze your route usage and recommend which routes to turn off storage for, or to shorten retention windows.
[12:50] Jenna: example: for chat support logs, Optimize suggested reducing retention from 90 to 7 days and enabling prefix caching; this saved 23% of storage and reduced token cost by ~12% in that customer's workload.
[13:12] Mike: can Optimize run on a sample dataset we provide? like if we give traces, can it generate recommendations?
[13:20] Jenna: yes, upload or share traces (sanitized or via our audit-mode) and Optimize will run a workload analysis. for PII-heavy routes we recommend audit-mode first.
[13:40] Daniel: what about multi-tenant setups \u2014 are policies per-tenant? we have sub-products with different compliance needs.
[13:48] Jenna: policies are hierarchical: global tenant, sub-tenant, route. you can lock policies at higher levels. for Dedicated you can scope per-customer within your org.
[14:10] Victor: question on data plane encryption-in-flight between our services and Redwood. do you support mTLS?
[14:18] Jenna: yes we support TLS 1.2/1.3, mTLS for Private/Dedicated endpoints, and we can configure client cert requirements for stricter setups.
[14:35] Priya: does redaction run before anything is ever persisted? i.e., is there any window where raw data is written and then redaction post-processed?
[14:45] Jenna: redaction is part of the ingest pipeline and runs prior to write. in the hosted path we do short-lived in-memory processing; raw data is not persisted. for added assurance we can enable an "ingest-only" ephemeral-mode during PoC that logs only detection results, not content.
[15:10] [16:00] Jenna: demo of API call. curl -X POST to https://api.redwood.sh/v1/generate with body {"input":"..." , "store_requests": false, "redact": "auto"} \u2014 response returns id and typical tokens.
[15:40] Victor: does the telemetry for model performance include any content?
[15:45] Jenna: telemetry is aggregated metrics; trace ids may link to metadata but not to request content if storage is off.
[16:05] Mike: legal follow-up \u2014 we might need written confirmation that if we set store_requests=false for a route, Redwood support cannot access the raw content.
[16:15] Samir: we can include that wording and the support access controls in the security pack \u2014 for hosted there's a small caveat around incident debugging where ephemeral content may be accessed by engineers with just-in-time access and audit. we'll detail protections.
[16:40] Priya: do you have examples of regexes or recommended patterns for card numbers and account ids?
[16:48] Jenna: yes \u2014 we have a patterns library in the Console and sample policy JSON. i'll attach that. for cards we recommend Luhn-check-enabled regex plus length checks.
[17:05] Daniel: any limitations with streaming responses and redaction? like if PII appears mid-stream?
[17:15] Jenna: streaming redaction is supported; we buffer a small sliding window to catch spans. if you need strict realtime zero-echo we recommend route-level store_requests=false and client-side filtering prior to submit.
[17:40] Victor: how about rate-limited exports to our S3 \u2014 can they be async?
[17:48] Jenna: yes, exports are scheduled; you can configure daily/weekly push or on-demand. we also support a webhook that notifies your ingestion pipeline when a new export is available.
[18:05] Samir: switching to questions from Sara (legal). Sara: is there any legal/contractual language around data residency we should be aware of?
[18:12] Sara: we need to ensure EU data never leaves region for EU-subtenants.
[18:18] Jenna: we support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated \u2014 you can pin to eu-west-1 and we'll ensure data storage and processing happens in the region. Private of course stays inside your network.
[18:40] Sara: also need to confirm we can get SOC2 attestation and pen-test reports.
[18:46] Samir: yes, SOC2 Type II report is available; pen test summary included. i'll send the package.
[19:05] Mike: technical deep dive \u2014 if we run a benchmark for latency, how do you recommend we measure impact of redaction?
[19:12] Jenna: run comparison with store_requests on vs off, and with redaction auto vs off. collect p95 latency, CPU, and accelerator utilization. we'll help with a harness and can provide a baseline dataset and agent container.
[19:40] Daniel: is there any difference between hosted/managed vs Dedicated in terms of feature parity for these controls?
[19:47] Jenna: feature parity is high; Dedicated exposes more controls for key mgmt, mTLS, and local logging. Hosted has the same toggles but uses envelope encryption. Private gives full control.
[20:10] Priya: about role separation \u2014 can we prevent support from retrieving unredacted content? what about emergency access?
[20:18] Jenna: support access can be blocked; we have a just-in-time access model with approvals and full audit trail. customers can request locked mode where support cannot access request bodies.
[20:40] Samir: quick recap of the PoC plan: provision a tenant, set three routes to store_requests=false, run a 2-week load test with the ingestion check, run Optimize on the sample traces, provide security pack. any objections?
[20:58] Mike: that sounds right. timeline?
[21:02] Samir: propose kickoff 2026-03-16. jenna will share config and recording by 2026-03-07, security docs by 2026-03-08.
[21:20] Sara: we may need additional legal review \u2014 i'll review the pack.
[21:30] Victor: small nit \u2014 do you support masking in the UI when viewing traces? i want to ensure devs can't accidentally paste content in tickets.
[21:38] Jenna: yes, UI supports masked view and a show/hide toggle restricted by role.
[22:00] [25:00] Customer Q&A continues \u2014 Priya asks about integration with our internal SIEM; Jenna confirms webhook and bulk export support.
[25:30] Priya: what happens during a model rollback \u2014 do you preserve old policy behavior?
[25:38] Jenna: policy versions are decoupled from model versions; rollbacks don't affect retention rules.
[26:05] Daniel: can Optimize suggest quantization or batching changes to reduce cost while preserving redaction behavior?
[26:15] Jenna: yes, Optimize suggests quantization profiles for local Dedicated GPUs and batching knobs; it ensures KV cache and model behavior remain intact.
[26:40] Mike: any customer references in financial space we can talk to?
[26:48] Samir: we can provide references after NDA; we have a payments customer who did a similar PoC \u2014 i'll confirm names and get permission.
[27:10] [30:00] Live demo wrap-up \u2014 Jenna shows policy audit log, version history, sample export to S3.
[30:30] Priya: one more question \u2014 can we redact across multiple fields atomically? like name + account number in same pass?
[30:38] Jenna: yes, our detector supports multi-span redaction and ordered regex application. you can also chain rules for dependent redactions.
[31:05] Sara: in the event of a legal hold, can we suspend deletion?
[31:12] Samir: we support legal hold flags that prevent TTL enforcement for specified request ids \u2014 those are recorded in audit logs and require admin-level permission.
[31:40] Victor: do you have a sample CSV of fields to send to Optimize?
[31:46] Jenna: yes, sample schema: route, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, storage_bytes, retention_days. i'll attach the sample.
[32:10] [40:00] Longer technical discussion on PII false positives/negatives and tuning. Jenna mentions running a two-phase approach: audit-mode then live redact with backfill.
[36:00] Priya: any edge cases where binary blobs (attachments) get scanned?
[36:08] Jenna: attachments are base64 encoded; we support scanning text attachments but not arbitrary binaries. for attachments we recommend pre-processing and stripping sensitive files client-side.
[36:40] Mike: access controls for exports \u2014 can we restrict which service accounts can request an export?
[36:48] Jenna: yes, export permissions are RBAC controlled and require multi-sig approval for large exports.
[37:15] [45:00] Final checks \u2014 Jenna reiterates the sample config and audit-mode plan.
[45:30] Daniel: from product POV, we'll want to evaluate developer experience for toggles and the API surface \u2014 victor and I will try the SDK.
[45:45] Victor: i'll load the sample workload and report p95/p99.
[46:00] Samir: i'll follow up with the security pack and schedule kickoff.
[46:15] Mike: thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
[46:30] Priya: thanks \u2014 one ask: include the ingestion-check script and the exact curl examples in the repo.
[46:38] Jenna: will do, adding to next steps.
[47:10] [55:00] Wrap-up \u2014 Samir summarizes: send security docs, demo recording, config JSON; schedule PoC kickoff 2026-03-16; customer to send three sensitive routes and workload traces.
[55:30] Samir: thanks all \u2014 we'll follow up in email.

Notes: transcription contains occasional offsets and name typos; some technical terms like KV cache were mentioned in passing (kv-cache). References: sent items will include security whitepaper, SOC2, pen-test summary, sample policy JSON, ingestion check script, Optimize sample schema.
